question: Mayonnaise is mostly oil, plus vinegar and yolk, all runny liquids. What mainly lets it hold a peak?
options: The egg yolk setting like custard
The mustard's starch thickening the water
The oil droplets crammed against each other
answer: The oil droplets crammed against each other. Round droplets can fill at most about 74% of a space; beyond that they flatten into many-sided cells, and any flow must deform them. At 75 to 80% oil, mayonnaise is packed oil cells in thin films of water. Whisk in more oil and it stiffens further.
move: Crowding alone can turn a crowd of liquids into a solid.
ask: Which small habits in my life are solid only because they are crowded together?
trap: Egg is the famous ingredient, so it seems to do the thickening.
reference: McClements, Food Emulsions: Principles, Practices, and Techniques, 2nd edition, CRC Press, 2005
